content:
A Kenya tour package from India works best as a private 6 to 7-day road safari: a nonstop Mumbai flight to Nairobi, Amboseli for elephants under Kilimanjaro, the Rift Valley lakes and three nights in the Masai Mara. Budget about ₹3 lakh per person with flights, or about ₹1.3 lakh for a shared 4-day trip.

Most Indian packages online show a fixed rupee price and little else. This guide is written from our Nairobi office for travellers comparing a Kenya tour package from India with what the trip really involves: flights from Indian cities, the eTA, the yellow fever rule on the way home, vegetarian and Jain food, and the months that suit Indian school and festival holidays. Browse all our Kenya safari packages as you read.

Quick Facts

  • Flight: Mumbai to Nairobi nonstop in about 6.5 hours with IndiGo, Kenya Airways or Air India (checked November 2026)
  • Entry: Kenya eTA from US$30 plus compulsory Kenyan health cover of about US$44
  • Health: Yellow fever certificate needed to re-enter India, taken 10+ days before you fly home
  • Time difference: Kenya is 2.5 hours behind India
  • Best months: July to October for the migration; January to March for dry weather and better prices
  • Budget: about ₹1.3 lakh (4-day shared) to ₹3 lakh (7-day private) per person, flights included

How do you fly from India to Kenya?

Mumbai is India's gateway to Kenya. IndiGo, Kenya Airways and Air India all fly nonstop from Mumbai to Nairobi, a journey of about six and a half hours, with roughly 19 to 23 nonstop departures a week listed in November 2026.

Flights are the biggest variable in a Kenya tour package from India. Return economy fares from Mumbai that we saw in late November 2026 started at about ₹40,000, and July, August and Diwali dates sell out first. Book on IndiGo, Kenya Airways or Air India directly, or send us your city and we will suggest the best connection.

Flying from Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai or Kolkata

Travellers outside Mumbai usually connect once, through Mumbai or a Gulf hub such as Dubai, Doha or Abu Dhabi. Air India's own Delhi route page advertises a Delhi to Nairobi service, but its live search showed only one-stop options when we checked in November 2026, so confirm the current schedule before you book the ground part of your Kenya tour package from India.

Kenya is two and a half hours behind India. With the long transfer from home to the airport, most of our Indian guests rest one night in Nairobi and start the safari the next morning.

What does a Kenya tour package from India cost?

The Kenya tour package from India we sell most costs about ₹2.5 lakh per person for our private 7-day safari before flights, and about ₹3 lakh once you add the Mumbai fare, entry fees and tips. The shared 4-day budget safari starts near ₹82,000 on the ground.

Our trip prices are set in US dollars. We converted them at the Bank of England spot rate of ₹92.915 to US$1 on 23 November 2026 (USD to INR reference rates). These are planning figures from low-season starting prices; your quote moves with dates and lodge availability.

What the 7-day package includes

The private 7-day Kenya tour package from India runs in a 4WD Land Cruiser with an English-speaking driver guide: two nights in Amboseli, a boat ride on Lake Naivasha, one night at Lake Nakuru and three nights in the Mara. Lodges, park fees, full board meals, a Maasai village visit and the Giraffe Centre are included.

Not included in this Kenya tour package from India are international flights, the eTA, insurance, drinks, tips and the optional Masai Mara balloon flight at US$500 (about ₹46,500) per person.

Kenya eTA and yellow fever rules for Indian passports

Indian passport holders need an approved Kenya eTA before flying, and a valid yellow fever certificate to get back into India. Sort both before you pay the final balance on any Kenya tour package from India.

The Kenya eTA and health insurance

Apply on the official Kenya eTA website up to three months before travel; the fee starts at US$30 (checked November 2026). You upload your passport, a photo, your return flight and a hotel booking or our confirmation letter. Since October 2026 you also buy the compulsory Kenyan travel health insurance, about US$44, inside the same application.

That Kenyan cover is only the entry minimum, so keep your own travel insurance for cancellation, baggage and medical evacuation. Our Kenya eTA guide walks through the form step by step.

Yellow fever on the way home

This is the rule that catches Indian travellers out. India's Ministry of Health yellow fever guidance lists Kenya as an endemic country and requires a valid certificate on arrival; without one you can be quarantined for up to six days (checked November 2026). The High Commission of India in Nairobi confirms the vaccine must be taken at least 10 days before travel to India.

Get the jab at a government-authorised centre in India (the ministry lists a fee of ₹300 a dose), and carry the original card, because photocopies and phone images lead to quarantine. See our yellow fever requirements page and the Kenya safari vaccinations post for malaria advice too.

Can you eat vegetarian or Jain food on safari?

Vegetarian food is easy to arrange on a Kenya tour package from India, and Jain food is possible with planning. Lodges on our routes cook on full board, and their chefs are used to vegetarian guests.

Tell us at booking whether you eat eggs, onion, garlic or root vegetables. We write the list to each lodge, request a dal-and-rice option at dinner, and pack fruit and snacks for game drives. Halal meals can be arranged the same way for Muslim guests on a Kenya tour package from India.

When is the best time for a Kenya safari from India?

July to October is the best time for most Indian travellers, because the Great Migration herds are usually in the Masai Mara. January to March is the strongest alternative, with dry weather and lower lodge prices, while April and May bring the long rains.

Our great migration month by month guide shows where the herds usually are each week. If Diwali is your only window, a Kenya tour package from India built around Amboseli, Lake Nakuru and the Mara conservancies still gives strong game viewing even after the herds move on.

Which Kenya safari suits Indian families and groups?

Indian families booking a Kenya tour package from India often travel with grandparents and children, so pace and vehicle space matter more than ticking off parks. Our private road safaris suit this well, because the vehicle stops when anyone needs a break.

Choosing the right Kenya tour package from India for your group

For a first visit with elders, the 6-day Kenya family safari keeps drives shorter with a midday rest in Amboseli and a walk on Crescent Island. Groups of 8 to 12 usually take two Land Cruisers so everyone has a window seat. Couples can fly to the Mara in about an hour on the 3-day Masai Mara fly-in safari instead of driving.

Insider Tips

  • Book the jab early: authorised centres get busy before the July to October peak, so get the certificate before you even apply for the eTA
  • Carry dollars: clean, recent, undamaged US dollar notes for tips and extras; rupees are not exchanged in the parks
  • Pack snacks: dry fruit, nuts and home snacks travel well and help on the five to six-hour Mara drive
  • Pick a lodge with a kitchen briefing: we send your dietary list to every lodge in writing, but remind the manager on arrival too
  • Keep one Nairobi night: a rest night after the flight makes the first long drive to Amboseli or the Mara much easier for elders and children

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a Kenya tour package from India cost?

A Kenya tour package from India costs about ₹3 lakh per person for a private 7-day road safari, including a ₹40,000 Mumbai return fare, the eTA, Kenyan health insurance and tips. A shared 4-day budget safari comes to roughly ₹1.3 lakh all in. July to October and Diwali dates cost more.

Is there a direct flight from India to Kenya?

Yes. IndiGo, Kenya Airways and Air India fly nonstop from Mumbai to Nairobi, and the flight takes about six and a half hours (checked November 2026). Travellers from Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai or Kolkata usually connect through Mumbai or a Gulf hub, so check the live schedule for your city before you pay for the safari.

Do Indians need a visa for Kenya?

Indian passport holders do not need a traditional visa for a Kenya holiday, but every traveller, children included, needs an approved electronic travel authorisation (eTA) before flying. The official site lists the fee from US$30, and since October 2026 you also buy the Kenyan travel health insurance, about US$44, during the same application.

Do I need a yellow fever vaccine to return to India from Kenya?

Yes. India's Ministry of Health requires a valid yellow fever certificate from anyone arriving from Kenya, and the vaccine must be taken at least 10 days before you land back in India. Without it you can be quarantined for up to six days. Carry the original card, because photocopies and phone images are not accepted.

Can I get vegetarian and Jain food on a Kenya safari?

Yes, vegetarian food is easy on a Kenya safari because lodges on our routes serve full board and cook to order when told in advance. Jain meals without onion, garlic or root vegetables are possible too, but we write the rules to each lodge before you arrive and pack some ready snacks for long drives.

Final Thoughts

A good Kenya tour package from India is simple once three things are in place: a nonstop Mumbai flight, an approved eTA with Kenyan health cover, and a yellow fever card for the trip home. Pick July to October for the migration or January to March for value.
